title: Frictionless ops rapid update and Q&A prep
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad to shape a short, verbal update for the Friday ops sync and prep two-paragraph internal comms (email + slack) about the weekend soft-handoff mode. Not formal — intend to copy/paste into the sync notes and then iterate with Lena/Marcus.

Audience: ops rotation, SRE PD, product on-call contacts, leadership FYI. Keep it ~2–3 minutes to read/say. Focus: what changes, why, what to expect, what not to worry about.

Topline message (one sentence): We are enabling the frictionless weekend handoff mode this weekend — brief change in routing rules and reduced noncritical deploys to improve on-call predictability; no customer-facing downtime expected.

Key bullets for the verbal update (in order):
- Why: repeated noise during low-usage periods and cascading retries from background jobs created unnecessary wakeups; we’re trying a smoother handoff to reduce pager churn.
- What we change: enable routing tier floor, disable nonblocking batch job retries between 02:00–08:00 PT, and switch traffic fallback from regional to global-standby model.
- Impact: no model retirement or feature toggles — requests still served; small increase (~5–12ms) tail latency for a tiny subset of large context generations that would otherwise trigger cross-region fallback.
- Monitoring & rollback: golden metrics (p50/p95 latency, token rate, error budget burn) instrumented; automatic rollback if error budget burn > 3% in any 30m window.
- Who to call: on-call rotation + Alex (eng-sre lead) as second. Slack channel: #ops-weekend-handovers (post link in comms).

Draft slack/email (short):
Subject: Weekend handoff: frictionless mode — what to expect
Hi team —
We’re running a short experiment this weekend to smooth on-call handoffs. From 02:00–08:00 PT Sat–Sun we’ll:
  • enable routing-tier floor to prefer local capacity
  • disable nonblocking job retries that can cascade
  • move fallback routing to global-standby for constrained capacity
No customer-visible downtime expected. We instrumented p50/p95 latency, token throughput, and error budget; automated rollback is configured. Please raise any immediate concerns in #ops-weekend-handovers.
Thanks,
Kai (on behalf of eng-sre)

Q&A cheat sheet (likely questions & short answers):
Q: Will this affect Dedicated/Private customers?
A: No configuration changes for Dedicated tenants or Private installs — this is a hosted routing policy experiment only.

Q: Could this increase errors for heavy-generation customers?
A: We expect a very small set of long-generation requests to see faintly higher tail latency; errors should not increase thanks to our fallback protections and cache priming.

Q: How fast can we revert?
A: Rollback is automated via a runbook; manual rollback path is ~5 minutes if automation fails.

Q: Who needs to be paged?
A: Only if error budget exceeds threshold; on-call will triage and call Alex if escalation needed.

Open/TO‑DO (notes to self):
- Confirm that the runbook links are up-to-date (runbook id: confluence:frictionless-ops-runbook-v2).
- Add a note to the routing config PR that fallback change is temporary and flagged (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/321).
- Validate metrics dashboards include the new fallback metric (global-fallback-rate).
- Draft a 1-paragraph follow-up that summarizes learnings and triage events on Monday if there’s any visible change.

Risks/mitigations (one-liners for leadership):
- Risk: short-term increase in tail latency for rare generation paths; mitigation: small traffic segment and automatic rollback.
- Risk: noisy alerts from newly instrumented fallback metric; mitigation: suppress nonactionable alerts for 24h and tune thresholds next week.

Notes to self: keep tone calm and operational — avoid technical jargon in leadership note. Iterate with Lena for wording on the customer-facing snippet (she has better phrasing). Marcus will sanity-check the rollback automation tomorrow morning.

End of scratchpad.

(If I turn this into the final comms, copy the Items under "Draft slack/email" and strip the bracketed dev links before posting.)
